item.title: Mistrial declared in Daniel Perry deadly conduct case due to jury issues
item.description: On Monday, jury selection will begin in the misdemeanor deadly conduct case against Daniel Perry, who was pardoned in 2024 after a jury convicted him in 2023 of the murder of a protester on July 25, 2020.

item.title: Wildfire evacuations near Bastrop State Park lifted; 46-acre fire now 75% contained
item.description: A mandatory evacuation was issued for cabins in Bastrop State Park and the Pines at Bastrop RV Park after a wildfire began Sunday night, but it was lifted early Monday morning, according to the Texas A&amp;M Forest Service.

item.title: MoPac South Project public meeting Tuesday
item.description: The Central Texas Regional Mobility Authority is holding a public meeting on Tuesday to discuss the MoPac South Project, which would add an express toll lane in each direction from downtown Austin to Slaughter Lane, with a price tag of around $824 million.

item.title: Austin airport unveils renderings, new details about 'Concourse M'
item.description: When Austin-Bergstrom International Airport officials unveiled their design plans for a new terminal, they also introduced 'Concourse M' — another new terminal space featuring six gates. Now, we're getting our first look at the planned space.

item.title: Vance visits Austin for fundraiser with $50,000 cover charge
item.description: Vice President J.D. Vance is traveling to Austin to attend a fundraising event hosted by Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale, where donors must pledge $50,000 or more, while Texas State Rep. Christina Morales criticizes Vance for focusing on wealthy tech billionaires instead of working families.

item.title: LaGuardia crash 'the very kind of catastrophe' Rep. Doggett fears could happen in Austin
item.description: When asked about the fatal crash between a plane and fire truck at LaGuardia Airport, Congressman Lloyd Doggett minced no words in his response: "It's the very kind of catastrophe that I fear we could have here in Austin."

item.title: Ballot Proposition that could bring more electronic billboards to Round Rock
item.description: Round Rock voters will decide in May whether to expand the presence of electronic billboards (EMCs) across the city.

item.title: Texas heads to Fort Worth, takes on SEC foe in Sweet 16
item.description: The Longhorns and Wildcats will meet March 28 at Dickies Arena in Fort Worth, and while the time has yet to be determined, it'll be an earlier game at either 11:30 a.m. or 2 p.m. The specific tip time should be announced after all second-round games are completed Monday night.

item.title: Unseasonably warm through the end of March
item.description: We hoped you liked yesterday's weather... because today will look and feel very similar... and the next day... and the next. -Meteorologist Kristen Currie

item.title: These are the best places to live in the US for 2026, study finds
item.description: What is the ideal place to live in the United States? A new study claims to have the answer.

item.title: No green thumb? Try Texas' new Wild Thumb app
item.description: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation has launched a new mobile app called "Wild Thumb" to help residents incorporate native plants into their yards and gardens.

item.title: SH 130 to become test route for new driverless freight trucks
item.description: The future of freight is speeding toward reality quicker than you might think, and it's happening right in Austin's own backyard.

item.title: Plans to return to countywide voting for runoff in Williamson County
item.description: During the March primary, many Williamson County voters encountered long lines and confusion after the county reverted to precinct‑specific voting on Election Day — a change several residents said they didn’t know about.
